850.subject: Chemistry
850.text:
Assertion : F - F bond has low bond dissociation energy.
Reason : The fluorine has lower reactivity.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
850.sol:
Lower value of bond dissociation energy of fluorine is due to the high inter electronic repulsions between non-bonding electrons of the $2 p$-orbital of small sized fluorine. As a result $\mathrm{F}-\mathrm{F}$ bond is weaker as comparison to $\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{Cl} and \mathrm{Br}-\mathrm{Br}$ bonds.

$\begin{array}{lr}& \text{ Bond dissociation energy }$\\
$\mathrm{F}-\mathrm{F}& 38 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{cal}/ \mathrm{mole}$\\
$\mathrm{Cl}-\mathrm{Cl}& 57 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{cal}/ \mathrm{mole}$\\
$\mathrm{Br}-\mathrm{Br}& 45.5 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{cal}/ \mathrm{mole}$\\
$\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{I}& 35.6 \mathrm{~K} \mathrm{cal}/ \mathrm{mole}
\end{array}$
850.meta: Assertion : F - F bond has low bond dissociation energy. Reason : The fluorine has lower reactivity.

1684.text: The displacement of a body is given to be proportional to the cube of time elapsed. The magnitude of the acceleration of the body is proportional to
1684.sol:
Here, $s \propto t^3$
or $s=k t^3$
velocity, $v=\frac{d s}{d t}=\frac{d}{d t}\left(k t^3\right)=3 k t^2$
Acceleration, $a=\frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{d}{d t}\left(3 k t^2\right)=6 k t$
$\therefore a \propto t$

Given, $x^2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)-y^2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)=K$
Differentiate with respect to $x$, we get.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{x^2 d \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}{d x}+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) \frac{d\left(x^2\right)}{d x}-\frac{y^2 d \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)}{d x} \\
& -\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) \frac{d\left(y^2\right)}{d x}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2\left(\frac{x^2}{x^2+y^2}\right)\left(\frac{x \frac{d y}{d x}-y}{x^2}\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) 2 x \\
& -y^2\left(\frac{y^2}{x^2+y^2}\right)\left(\frac{y \cdot \frac{-x d y}{d x}}{y^2}\right)-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) 2 y=0 \\
& \Rightarrow\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(1 \cdot y_1(1,1)-1\right)+\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1}\right) \cdot 2 \\
& -\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(1-y_1(1,1)\right)-\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{1}\right) \cdot 2=0
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(y_1\left(1_1, 1\right)-1\right)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y_1(1,1)=1 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}(1,1)=1\end{aligned}$

Two statements [A] and [B] are given below. Choose the correct option.
A) Protonated R$-$CH_2-$OH can serve as Electrophiles while neutral R$-$OH acts as a Nucleophile. \\ B) The bond between O$-$H cleaves when R$-$CH_2-$OH acts as Electrophiles and the bond between C$-$O cleaves when they act as Nucleophiles.
options: Both the statements [A] and [B] are wrong
Statement [A] is correct but [B] is wrong
Both the statements [A] and [B] are correct
Statement [B] is correct but [A] is wrong
19474.sol:
Alcohols can act as both nucleophiles and electrophiles.

Neutral alcohols act as nucleophiles due to the presence of lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom. In these reactions, the O$-$H bond is cleaved.

Protonated alcohols act as electrophiles because protonation makes the hydroxyl group a good leaving group (H_2$O). In these reactions, a nucleophile attacks the carbon atom, and the C$-$O bond is cleaved. \\ \\ Statement [A] is correct as protonated R$-$CH_2-$OH acts as an electrophile and neutral R$-$OH acts as a nucleophile.

Statement [B] is incorrect because the C$-$O bond cleaves when alcohols act as electrophiles, and the O$-$H bond cleaves when they act as nucleophiles.

Answer: Statement [A] is correct but [B] is wrong

19519.text: The major product in the given reaction is
19519.sol:
The reaction of phenol with zinc dust under heating conditions is a standard reduction reaction.

When phenol (C_{6}H_{5}OH$) is heated with zinc dust, the zinc acts as a reducing agent and removes the oxygen atom from the hydroxyl group to form zinc oxide (ZnO$).

The chemical equation for this reaction is:
$C_{6}H_{5}OH + Zn \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_{6}H_{6} + ZnO$

The product formed is benzene.

Answer: benzene

19788.subject: Chemistry
19788.text: Which of the following pairs of ions in iso-electronic and iso-structural?
19788.sol:
Iso-electronic species have the same number of electrons, and iso-structural species have the same geometry and hybridization.

For $\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}$:
Total electrons = $6 + 3 \times 8 + 2 = 32$.
Hybridization: $\dfrac{1}{2}(4 + 0 + 2) = 3$ (sp$^2$ hybridization). Geometry: Trigonal planar.

For $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$:
Total electrons = $7 + 3 \times 8 + 1 = 32$.
Hybridization: $\dfrac{1}{2}(5 + 0 + 1) = 3$ (sp$^2$ hybridization). Geometry: Trigonal planar.

Since both $\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$ have 32 electrons and sp$^2$ hybridized trigonal planar structures, they are both iso-electronic and iso-structural.

Answer: $\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}, \mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$

19960.subject: Chemistry
19960.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
19960.text: Arrange the following ions in the decreasing order of their ionic radii: $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}, \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}, \mathrm{S}^{2-}, \mathrm{K}^{+}$
19960.sol:
The given ions are $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$, $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$, and $\mathrm{K}^{+}$.

First, determine the number of electrons in each ion:
$\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ has $16 + 2 = 18$ electrons.
$\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ has $17 + 1 = 18$ electrons.
$\mathrm{K}^{+}$ has $19 - 1 = 18$ electrons.
$\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ has $20 - 2 = 18$ electrons.

All these ions are isoelectronic, meaning they have the same number of electrons (18$).

For isoelectronic species, the ionic radius decreases as the nuclear charge (atomic number, $Z$) increases, because a higher nuclear charge pulls the same number of electrons more strongly towards the nucleus.

The atomic numbers are:
\mathrm{S} (Z = 16)$
$\mathrm{Cl} (Z = 17)$
$\mathrm{K} (Z = 19)$
$\mathrm{Ca} (Z = 20)$

Arranging them in decreasing order of ionic radii based on increasing atomic number:
$\mathrm{S}^{2-} (Z=16) > \mathrm{Cl}^{-} (Z=17) > \mathrm{K}^{+} (Z=19) > \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} (Z=20)$.

Answer: $\mathrm{S}^{2-} > \mathrm{Cl}^{-} > \mathrm{K}^{+} > \mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$

20127.subject: Chemistry
20127.text:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Choose the right option.
Assertion: The Molar conductivity of KCl increases very slowly with dilution and approaches a limiting value when dilution is infinite.
Reason: In case of KCl there is an increase in the number of ions on dilution due to complete ionisation at infinite dilution.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
20127.sol:
KCl is a strong electrolyte and is completely ionised in solution at all concentrations. Therefore, the number of ions does not increase upon dilution.

The molar conductivity of a strong electrolyte like KCl increases slowly with dilution and approaches a limiting value at infinite dilution (\Lambda_m^{{}^{\circ}}$). This increase is not due to an increase in the number of ions, but rather due to a decrease in interionic attractions, which increases the mobility of the ions.

Thus, the Assertion is correct, but the Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect$

Target pH $= 4\Rightarrow[H^+] = 10^{-4}$ M, meaning solution is acidic \Rightarrow practically all $ OH^-$ must be removed.

Anodic reaction: $4OH^- \to O_2 + 2H_2O + 4e^-$

1 mole of $OH^-$ releases 1 mole of electrons $\Rightarrown_e = 0.01$ mol

$Q = n_e \times F = 0.01 \times 96500 = 965$ C

$t = \dfrac{Q}{I} = \dfrac{965}{0.5} = 1930\ s = 1.93 \times 10^3\ s$

20933.subject: Mathematics
20933.text: Oil from a conical funnel is dripping at the rate of $5 \mathrm{ cm}^3 / \mathrm{s}$. If the radius and height of the funnel are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively, then the rate at which the oil level drops when it is 5 cm from the top is
20933.sol:
Let $R = 10$ cm be the radius and $H = 20$ cm be the height of the conical funnel. Let $r$ and $h$ be the radius and height of the oil level at any time $t$. By similar triangles, $\dfrac{r}{h} = \dfrac{R}{H} = \dfrac{10}{20} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $r = \dfrac{h}{2}$.

The volume of the oil in the funnel is $V = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi r^2 h = \dfrac{1}{3} \pi \left( \dfrac{h}{2} \right)^2 h = \dfrac{\pi h^3}{12}$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{12} \times 3h^2 \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi h^2}{4} \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -5$ cm$^3$/s (since the volume is decreasing). The oil level is 5 cm from the top, so the height of the oil from the vertex is $h = 20 - 5 = 15$ cm.

Substituting the values, $-5 = \dfrac{\pi (15)^2}{4} \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{225 \pi}{4} \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

Solving for $\dfrac{dh}{dt}$, we get $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = -5 \times \dfrac{4}{225 \pi} = -\dfrac{20}{225 \pi} = -\dfrac{4}{45 \pi}$ cm/s.

Answer: $-\dfrac{4}{45 \pi} \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$

22675.subject: Physics
22675.text: The stopping potential when a metal surface is illuminated by light of wavelength $\lambda$ is 15 V. The stopping potential when the same surface is illuminated by light of wavelength $4 \lambda$ is 3 V. The ratio of threshold wavelength to the initial incident wavelength $\lambda$ is:
22675.sol:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation, the stopping potential $V_s$ is given by $eV_s = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \Phi$, where $\Phi$ is the work function of the metal and $\lambda_0$ is the threshold wavelength such that $\Phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$.

For the first case, $eV_1 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = 15e$. Thus, $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = 15e$ (Equation 1).

For the second case, $eV_2 = \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = 3e$. Thus, $\dfrac{hc}{4\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = 3e$ (Equation 2).

Subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:

$\left( \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{4\lambda} \right) = 15e - 3e = 12e$

$\dfrac{3hc}{4\lambda} = 12e \Rightarrow \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = 16e$.

Substituting $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = 16e$ into Equation 1:

$16e - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = 15e \Rightarrow \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = e$.

Since $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = 16e$ and $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = e$, we have $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = 16 \left( \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} \right), which implies \dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{16}{\lambda_0}.

Therefore, \dfrac{\lambda_0}{\lambda} =16$, or the ratio of threshold wavelength to the initial wavelength is $16:1$.

Answer: $16: 1$

22808.subject: Physics
22808.text: A particle ' $X$ ' carrying a charge $+Q$ is moving in a circular path of radius $R$ around another particle ' $Y$ ' having a charge $-Q$ with a frequency ' $v$ '. Then the mass ' $m$ ' of the charged particle is
22808.sol:
The electrostatic force between the two charges $Q$ and $-Q$ separated by a distance $R$ provides the necessary centripetal force for the circular motion of particle $X$.

The electrostatic force is given by Coulomb's law as $F_{e} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Q^2}{R^2}$.

The centripetal force required for circular motion is $F_{c} = m \omega^2 R$, where $\omega$ is the angular frequency.

Given the frequency $v$, the angular frequency is $\omega = 2 \pi v$.

Equating the forces: $\dfrac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Q^2}{R^2} = m (2 \pi v)^2 R$.

Simplifying the equation: $\dfrac{Q^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 R^2} = m (4 \pi^2 v^2) R$.

Solving for mass $m$: $m = \dfrac{Q^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 R^2 (4 \pi^2 v^2 R)} = \dfrac{Q^2}{16 \pi^3 \varepsilon_0 R^3 v^2}$.

Answer: $M=\dfrac{Q^2}{\left[16 \pi^3 \varepsilon_0 R^3 v^2\right]}$

23569.text: A cylinder of fixed capacity 44.81 contains hydrogen gas at STP. What is the amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of the gas in the cylinder by $20^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ ? ($R=8.31 \mathrm{ J} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1} \mathrm{ K}^{-1}$)
23569.sol:
At STP, the volume of 1 mole of an ideal gas is $22.4 \text{ L}$.

Given the volume of the cylinder is $44.8 \text{ L}$, the number of moles $n$ of hydrogen gas is $n = \dfrac{44.8}{22.4} = 2 \text{ moles}$.

Hydrogen is a diatomic gas, so its molar heat capacity at constant volume $C_V$ is given by $C_V = \dfrac{f}{2}R$, where $f = 5$ is the degrees of freedom for a diatomic molecule.

$C_V = \dfrac{5}{2} \times 8.31 \text{ J mol}^{-1} \text{ K}^{-1} = 20.775 \text{ J mol}^{-1} \text{ K}^{-1}$.

The heat required $Q$ to raise the temperature by $\Delta T = 20^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C}$ (which is equivalent to $20 \text{ K}$) at constant volume is $Q = n C_V \Delta T$.

$Q = 2 \times 20.775 \times 20 = 40 \times 20.775 = 831 \text{ J}$.

Answer: 831 J

23605.text: In the expression $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{El}^2 \mathrm{ m}^{-5} \mathrm{G}^{-2}$ where $\mathrm{E}, 1, \mathrm{ m}$ and G represent Energy, Angular Momentum, Mass and Gravitational Constant, the dimensions of P are
23605.sol:
The dimensions of the given physical quantities are as follows:

Energy (E) = $[M^1 L^2 T^{-2}]$

Angular Momentum (l) = $[M^1 L^2 T^{-1}]$

Mass (m) = $[M^1]$

Gravitational Constant (G): From $F = G \dfrac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, we have $G = \dfrac{F r^2}{m^2} = \dfrac{[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}] [L^2]}{[M^2]} = [M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}]$

Now, substitute these dimensions into the expression $P = E l^2 m^{-5} G^{-2}$:

$P = [M^1 L^2 T^{-2}] \times ([M^1 L^2 T^{-1}])^2 \times ([M^1])^{-5} \times ([M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}])^{-2}$

$P = [M^1 L^2 T^{-2}] \times [M^2 L^4 T^{-2}] \times [M^{-5}] \times [M^2 L^{-6} T^4]$

Combine the powers of M, L, and T:

M: $1 + 2 - 5 + 2 = 0$

L: $2 + 4 + 0 - 6 = 0$

T: $-2 - 2 + 0 + 4 = 0$

Therefore, $P = [M^0 L^0 T^0]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^0 \mathrm{~T}^0\right]$

$\int_a^b \frac{x}{3\left[f(x)^2-1\right]} d x+b f(b)-a f(a)$

$-\int_a^b \frac{x}{3\left[(f(x))^2-1\right]} d x+b f(b)-a f(a)$

$\int_a^b \frac{x}{3\left[(f(x))^2-1\right]} d x-b f(b)+a f(a)$

$-\int_a^b \frac{x}{3\left[f(x)^2-1\right]} d x-b f(b)-a f(a)$
25285.sol:
Required area $=\int_a^b y d x=\int_a^b f(x) d x$
=[f(x) $\cdot$x]_a^b-\int_a^b f^{\prime}(x) $\cdot$x d x=b f(b)-a f(a)-\int_a^b f^{\prime}(x) $\cdot$x d x

=b f(b)-a f(a)+\int_a^b $\frac{x}{3\left[(f(x))^2-1\right]}$d x

As, $\quad f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{d y}{d x}=-\frac{1}{3\left(y^2-1\right)}=-\frac{1}{3\left[(f(x))^2-1\right]}$

26076.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
26076.text: A block of mass M has a circular cut with a frictionless surface as shown. The block rests on the horizontal frictionless surface of a fixed table. Initially the right edge of the block is at $x = 0$ , in a coordinate system fixed to the table. A point mass m is released from rest at the topmost point of the path as shown and it slides down. When the mass loses contact with the block its position is x and velocity is v. At that instant which of the following options is correct?
options: The velocity of the point mass m is $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gR}{1 + \dfrac{m}{M}}}$
The velocity of the block M is  $v =- \dfrac{m}{M}\sqrt{2gR}$
The position of the point mass is  $x = - \sqrt{2}\dfrac{mR}{m + M}$
The x component of displacement of the centre of the mass of block M is $- \dfrac{mR}{m + M}$
26076.sol:
When the centre of mass of the system is at origin,

${M}_{S}\Delta{\overset{-}{x}}_{cm} = {m}_{1}\Delta\overset{-}{x} + {m}_{2}\Delta{\overset{-}{x}}_{2}$

$0 = m\left(+ R + \overset{-}{x}\right) + m\overset{-}{x}$

$\overset{-}{x} = \dfrac{- mR}{M + m}$

The linear momentum of the system is conserved.

$0 = m{\overset{-}{v}}_{1} + M{\overset{-}{v}}_{2}$

${\overset{-}{v}}_{2} = - \dfrac{M{\overset{-}{v}}_{1}}{M}$

From energy conservation,

$mgR = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}_{2}^{2}$

$mgR = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}M{\left(\dfrac{m{v}_{1}}{M}\right)}^{2}$

$mgR = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{m}{M}\right)$

$\sqrt{\dfrac{2gR}{\left(1 + \dfrac{m}{M}\right)}} = {v}_{1}$

26684.text:
One mole of a monoatomic ideal gas goes through a thermodynamic cycle, as shown in the volume versus temperature $\left(V - T\right)$ diagram. The correct statement(s) is/are:
[ $R$ is the gas constant]
options: The ratio of heat transfer during processes  $1 \to 2$  and  $2 \to 3$  is  $\left|\dfrac{{Q}_{1 \to 2}}{{Q}_{2 \to 3}}\right| = \dfrac{5}{3}$
The ratio of heat transfer during processes  $1 \to 2$  and  $3 \to 4$  is  $\left|\dfrac{{Q}_{1 \to 2}}{{Q}_{3 \to 4}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{2}$
The above thermodynamic cycle exhibits only isochoric and adiabatic processes.
Work done in this thermodynamic cycle  $\left(1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 1\right)$  is  $\left|W\right| = \dfrac{1}{2}R{T}_{0}$

$\left(A\right) ⇒ \left|\dfrac{\Delta{Q}_{1 \to 2}}{\Delta{Q}_{2 \to 3}}\right| = \left|\dfrac{N{C}_{P}\Delta{T}_{1 \to 2}}{N{C}_{V}\Delta{T}_{2 \to 3}}\right| = \dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{V}} = \dfrac{5}{3} ⇒$ correct
$\left(B\right) ⇒ \left|\dfrac{\Delta{Q}_{1 \to 2}}{\Delta{Q}_{3 \to 4}}\right| = \dfrac{{T}_{0}}{{T}_{0} / 2} = 2 ⇒$ Incorrect
$( C ) ⇒$ No adiabatic process is involved $⇒$ incorrect
$( D ) ⇒$ Work done $=$ area inside $P - V$ diagram $= {P}_{0}{V}_{0} = nR\dfrac{{T}_{0}}{2}$ [at point $4$ in diagram] $⇒$ correct.
$1 \to 2 ⇒$ isobaric at pressure $2{P}_{0}$
$2 \to 3 ⇒$ isobaric at volume $2{V}_{0}$
$3 \to 4 ⇒$ isobaric at pressure ${P}_{0}$
$4 \to 1 ⇒$ isobaric at volume ${V}_{0}$
Given, number of moles, $n = 1$
and $r = \dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{V}} = \dfrac{5}{3}$ (for mono atomic gas)
Now, $\Delta{Q}_{1 \to 2}{=}^{n}{C}_{P} ( {T}_{2} - {T}_{1} )$
$= n ⋅ {C}_{p} ⋅ {T}_{0}$
$\Delta{Q}_{2 \to 3}{=}^{n}{C}_{V}\left({T}_{3} - {T}_{2}\right)$ = n ⋅ {C}_{V}$\left(- {T}_{2}\right)$
$\Delta{Q}_{3 \to 4} = n ⋅ {C}_{P}\left({T}_{4} - {T}_{3}\right) = n ⋅ {C}_{P}\left(\dfrac{- {T}_{0}}{2}\right)$

31308.subject: Chemistry
31308.text: X and Y are the number of electrons involved, respectively during the oxidation of $\mathrm{I}^{-}$to $\mathrm{I}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ to S by acidified $\mathrm{K}_{2} \mathrm{Cr}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{7}$. The value of $\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y}$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
31308.sol:
In acidic medium, $K_2Cr_2O_7$ acts as a strong oxidizing agent where $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is reduced to $Cr^{3+}$.
The reduction half-reaction is: $Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O$.
For the oxidation of $I^-$ to $I_2$:
The balanced oxidation half-reaction is $2I^- \rightarrow I_2 + 2e^-$.
To balance the electrons with the reduction half-reaction (6 electrons), we multiply the oxidation half-reaction by 3:
$6I^- \rightarrow 3I_2 + 6e^-$.
Thus, the number of electrons involved in the balanced redox reaction for $I^-$ oxidation is $X = 6$.
For the oxidation of $S^{2-}$ to $S$:
The balanced oxidation half-reaction is $S^{2-} \rightarrow S + 2e^-$.
To balance the electrons with the reduction half-reaction (6 electrons), we multiply the oxidation half-reaction by 3:
$3S^{2-} \rightarrow 3S + 6e^-$.
Thus, the number of electrons involved in the balanced redox reaction for $S^{2-}$ oxidation is $Y = 6$.
The value of $X + Y = 6 + 6 = 12$.

& \tan x=z \\
& \sec ^2 x d x=d z \\
& f(t)=2 \pi \int_0^{\infty} \frac{d z}{1+\sin ^2 t \cdot z^2} \\
& =\frac{\pi^2}{\sin t}
\end{aligned}$
Then $\int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\pi^2}{f(t)} d t \begin{aligned}
& =\int_0^{\pi / 2} \sin t d t \\
& =1

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3x - 5} \le 0\left(∵ 2{x}^{2} - 6x + 9 > 0 ∀ x \in R\right)$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \infty , \dfrac{5}{3}\right) . . . . . . \left(c\right)$

35400.text: Let ${e}_{1}$ be the eccentricity of the hyperbola $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{16} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{9} = 1$ and ${e}_{2}$ be the eccentricity of the ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1, a > b$, which passes through the foci of the hyperbola. If ${e}_{1}{e}_{2} = 1$, then the length of the chord of the ellipse parallel to the $x$-axis and passing through $( 0, 2 )$ is :
35400.sol:
The given equation of hyperbola is,  $H: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{16} - \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{9} = 1$

$⇒ {e}_{1} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{{3}^{2}}{{4}^{2}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{16 + 9}{16}}$

$⇒ {e}_{1} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

Foci of this hyperbola is given by, $F\left(\pm ae, 0\right).

$⇒ F$\left(\pm 5, 0\right)$

It is given that, ${e}_{1}{e}_{2} = 1$

$⇒ {e}_{2} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

Also, ellipse is passing through $( \pm 5, 0 )$

$⇒ \dfrac{{5}^{2}}{{a}^{2}} + \dfrac{0}{{b}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{25}{{a}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ {a}^{2} = 25$

$⇒ a = 5$

Now, ${e}_{2} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{5} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{25}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{16}{25} = 1 - \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{25}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{b}^{2}}{25} = \dfrac{9}{25}$

$⇒ {b}^{2} = 9$

$∴ a = 5 and b = 3$

$E: \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{9} = 1$

Putting, $y = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{4}{9} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{25} = \dfrac{5}{9}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} = \dfrac{125}{9}$

$⇒ x = \pm \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{3}$

So, end points of chord are $\left(\pm \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{3}, 2\right)$

Thus, length of chord $PQ$- is given by,

${L}_{PQ} = 2 \times \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{3}$

$⇒ {L}_{PQ} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{5}}{3}$

$∴ {T}_{n} = \left\{A \in S; {A}^{n\left(a + 1\right)} = I\right\}$

Now equation of family of circle will be,

${\left(x - \dfrac{8}{5}\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - \dfrac{6}{5}\right)}^{2} + \lambda\left(3x - 4y\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{3} + {y}^{3} + x\left(3\lambda - \dfrac{16}{5}\right) + y\left(- 4\lambda - \dfrac{12}{5}\right) + 4 = 0$

It touches $y$ axis so $2\sqrt{{f}^{2} - c} = 0 ⇒ {f}^{2} = c$

So,$\dfrac{{\left(4\lambda + \dfrac{12}{5}\right)}^{2}}{4} = 4$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{2}{5}$ or $\lambda = - \dfrac{8}{5}$

If, $\lambda = \dfrac{2}{5}, \text{then}r = 1$

Now sum of diameter will be ${d}_{1} + {d}_{2} = 2 \times 4 + 2 \times 1 = 10$

$⇒ \Delta = \left(6 + 8\sqrt{3}\right)$ sq. units.

If the mean of the following probability distribution of a random variable $\mathrm{X}$ :
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline \mathrm{X} & 0 & 2 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\
\hline \mathrm{P}$($\mathrm{X}) & a & 2 a & a+b & 2 b & 3 b \\

is $\frac{46}{9}$, then $ the variance of the distribution is$
37523.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & \sum P_i=1 \\ & a+2 a+a+b+2 b+3 b=1\end{aligned} 4 a+6 b=1$ ...(I)
$\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{x})=$ mean $=\frac{46}{9} \begin{aligned} & \sum P_i X_i=\frac{46}{9} \Rightarrow 4 a+4 a+4 b+12 b+24 b=\frac{46}{9} \\ & 8 a+40 b=\frac{46}{9}\end{aligned} 4 a+20 b=\frac{23}{9}$ ...(II)
Subtract (I) from (II) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{b}=\frac{1}{9} \& \mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{12} \\
& \text{ Variance }=\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}{ }^2\right)-\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2 \\
& \mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2=0^2 \times 9^2+2^2 \times 2 \mathrm{a}+4^2(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b})+6^2(2 \mathrm{ b})+8^2(3 \mathrm{ b}) \\
& =24 \mathrm{a}+280 \mathrm{ b}
\end{aligned}$Put $\mathrm{a}=\frac{1}{12} \quad \mathrm{ b}=\frac{1}{9} \begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}^2\right)=2+\frac{280}{9}=\frac{298}{9} \\
& \therefore \sigma^2=\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}^2\right)-\mathrm{E}\left(\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)^2 \\
& =\frac{298}{9}-\left(\frac{46}{9}\right)^2 \\
& \sigma^2=\frac{298}{9}-\frac{2116}{81} \\
& =\frac{566}{81}
\end{aligned}$

38099.sol:
${L}_{1} ≡ x = \dfrac{y}{2} = \dfrac{z}{3} = \lambda$ passes through $\left(0, 0, 0\right)$ and parallel to $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

${L}_{2} ≡ x - 1 = y - 3 = \dfrac{z - 1}{5} = \mu$ passes through $\left(1, 3, 1\right)$ and parallel to $\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

i.e. $\lambda = 1 + \mu, 2\lambda = 3 + \mu ⇒ \mu = 1$

Both the lines intersect at $\left(2, 4, 6\right)$

Normal to the plane will be $\left[\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5\end{cases}\right] = 7\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Since plane is parallel to both the given lines, the equation of the plane will be

$7\left(x - 2\right) - 2\left(y - 4\right) - \left(z - 6\right) = 0$

$⇒ 7x - 2y - z = 0$

38665.text: An angle between the lines whose direction cosines are given by the equations, $l+3 m+5 n=$ 0 and $5 l m-2 m n+6 n l=0$, is
38665.sol:
Given

$\begin{aligned}$&l+3 m+5 n=0 \\
&$\text{$ and }5 l m-2 m n+6 n l=0
\end{aligned}

From eq. (1) we have

l=-3 m-5 n

Put the value of$l$ in eq. (2), we get;

$\begin{aligned}$&5(-3 m-5 n) m-2 m n+6 n(-3 m-5 n)=0 \\
&\Rightarrow 15 m²+45 m n+30 n²=0 \\
&\Rightarrow m²+3 m n+2 n²=0 \\
&\Rightarrow m²+2 m n+m n+2 n²=0 \\
&\Rightarrow(m+n)(m+2 n)=0 \\
&\therefore m=-n $\text{$ or }m=-2 n \\
&$\text{$ For }m=-n, l=-2 n \\
&$\text{ And $for }m=-2 n, l=n
\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned}$&\therefore(l, m, n)=(-2 n,-n, n) $\text{$ Or }(l, m, n) \\
&=(n,-2 n, n) \\
&\Rightarrow(l, m, n)=(-2,-1,1)$\text{$ Or }(l, m, n) \\
&=(1,-2,1)
\end{aligned}

Therefore, angle between the lines is given as:$\begin{aligned}$&\cos ($\theta)=\frac{(-2)(1)+(-1) \cdot(-2)+(1)(1)}{\sqrt{6} \cdot \sqrt{6}}$\\
&\Rightarrow \cos ($\theta)=\frac{1}{6} \Rightarrow \theta=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)
\end{aligned}$

40080.text: The maximum velocity of the photoelectrons emitted from the surface is $v$ when light of frequency $n$ falls on a metal surface. If the incident frequency is increased to $3n$, the maximum velocity of the ejected photoelectrons will be:
40080.sol:
According to Einstein's photoelectric effect,

$K{E}_{max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - ϕ$

The incident energy of the photon is ${E}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = hn - ϕ . . . \left(1\right)$

If incident frequency increased to 3n

${E}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} = 3hn - ϕ$

$= 3\left(hn - ϕ\right) + 2ϕ$

${E}_{2} = 3{E}_{1} + 2ϕ$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}m{v}^{2} + 2ϕ$

$⇒ {v}_{2}^{2} = 3{v}^{2} + \dfrac{4ϕ}{m}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} > v\sqrt{3}$

40337.subject: Physics
40337.text:
The intensity of the light from a bulb incident on a surface is $0 . 22W{m}^{- 2}$. The amplitude of the magnetic field in this light-wave is _____ $\times {10}^{- 9}T$

(Given : Permittivity of vacuum ${ϵ}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}{C}^{2}{N}^{- 1}{m}^{- 2}$, speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{- 1}$)
40337.sol:
The intensity is defined as energy per unit time per unit area. Therefore, $I = \dfrac{dE}{Adt}$.

Energy density is energy per unit volume. Therefore, ${U}_{d} = \dfrac{dE}{Adx}$.

Dividing $\dfrac{I}{{U}_{d}} = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = c$

$⇒ {U}_{d} = \dfrac{I}{c} = \dfrac{0 . 22}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = \dfrac{22}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}J{m}^{- 3}$

Magnetic energy density will be half of total energy density, Therefore, ${U}_{b} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}J{m}^{- 3}$.

Now energy density in magnetic field is given by, ${U}_{b} = \dfrac{{B}^{2}}{2{\mu}_{0}}$. Therefore,

${B}_{rms}^{2}2{\mu}_{0} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}J{m}^{- 3}$ where ${B}_{rms}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{{B}_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = {B}_{0}^{2}2$

$⇒ {B}_{0}^{2}4{\mu}_{0} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10} ⇒ {B}_{0} = \sqrt{4 \times \left(4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\right) \times \dfrac{11}{3} \times {10}^{- 10}} ⇒ {B}_{0} = 4 . 29 \times {10}^{- 8}T ≃ 43 \times {10}^{- 9}T$

40888.subject: Physics
40888.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion $A$: A pendulum clock when taken to Mount Everest becomes fast.

Reason $R$: The value of g (acceleration due to gravity) is less at Mount Everest than its value on the surface of earth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $A$
$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct
$A$ is not correct but $R$ is correct
40888.sol:
Time period of a pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$, where $L$ is the length of the pendulum and $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity.

As, $T ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{g}}$, so the time period of vibration of the pendulum clock increases i.e. it starts taking more time to complete each vibration. Therefore, the pendulum clock becomes slow.

The acceleration due to gravity decreases with height $h \left(h ≪ R\right) above the surface as:

${g}^{'} = g$\left(1 - \dfrac{h}{R}\right)$

Thus, value of $g$ is less at Mount Everest than its value on the surface of earth.

Hence, assertion is wrong, but reason is correct.

42711.text: The general displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is $x = Asin\omegat$. Let $T$ be its time period. The slope of its potential energy ($U$) – time ($t$) curve will be maximum when $t = \dfrac{T}{\beta}$. The value of $\beta$ is ______.
42711.sol:
Given here, displacement $x = Asin\left(\omegat\right)$

Now, potential energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is $U = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\omega}^{2}{A}^{2}\sin^{2}\left(\omegat\right)$,

So, slope of potential energy and time curve is $\dfrac{dU}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{m{\omega}^{3}{A}^{2}}{2}sin2\omegat$

Now, ${\left(\dfrac{dU}{dt}\right)}_{max}$ will be maximum when $sin2\omegat = 1$

$⇒ 2\omegat = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}\right)t = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ t = \dfrac{T}{8} ⇒ \beta = 8$

42960.subject: Physics
42960.text: A $2$ meter long scale with least count of $0 . 2cm$ is used to measure the locations of objects on an optical bench. While measuring the focal length of a convex lens, the object pin and the convex lens are placed at $80cm$ mark and $1m$ mark, respectively. The image of the object pin on the other side of lens coincides with image pin that is kept at $180cm$ mark. The $%$ error in the estimation of focal length is:
42960.sol:
The formula for a lens is given by $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} . . . ( i )$

$u = \left(100 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm - \left(80 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm = \left(20 \pm 0 . 4\right)cm$

$v = \left(180 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm - \left(100 \pm 0 . 2\right)cm = \left(80 \pm 0 . 4\right)cm$

Substituting the values in the equation of focal length,

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{80} - \left(- \dfrac{1}{20}\right) = \dfrac{5}{80}$

$⇒ f = 16cm$

Differentiating the equation (i)

$\dfrac{df}{{f}^{2}} = \dfrac{dv}{{v}^{2}} + \dfrac{du}{{u}^{2}}$(Only positive sign is considered for error calculation)

$= \dfrac{0 . 4}{6400} + \dfrac{0 . 4}{400} = 0 . 4 \times \dfrac{17}{6400}$

$⇒ df = 0 . 4 \times \dfrac{17}{6400} \times {16}^{2} = 0 . 272$

The percentage error is

$\dfrac{df}{f} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 272}{16} \times 100 = 1 . 70 %$

43917.sol:

$Q\left(Heat\right) = 5000kcal = 5 \times {10}^{6}cal$

${T}_{2}\left(Sink\right) = {127}^{°}C = \left(127 + 273\right)K = 400K$

${T}_{1}\left(Source\right) = {727}^{°}C = \left(727 + 273\right)K = 1000K$

The efficiency of the Carnot cycle is given by,

$η = 1 - \dfrac{{T}_{sink}}{{T}_{source}} = \dfrac{W}{Q}$

$⇒ \left(1 - \dfrac{400}{1000}\right) = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{W}{5000}$$⇒ W = 3000kcal$

$= 3 \times \times 4 . 2 \times {10}^{6}J = 12 . 6 \times {10}^{6}J$.

44631.subject: Physics
44631.text: If momentum of a body is increased by $20 %$, then its kinetic energy increases by :
44631.sol:
A body of mass $m$, moving with momentum $p$ and kinetic energy $K$ are related as follows,
$K = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}$.
As the momentum of the body is increased by $20 %$, then its momentum becomes,
$\left(p + \dfrac{20}{100}p\right) = 1 . 2p$
and the mass of the body remains unchanged. So, kinetic energy is directly related to the square of momentum.

Hence, new kinetic energy $\left({K}^{'}\right)$ will be,
${K}^{'} = \dfrac{{\left(1 . 2p\right)}^{2}}{2m}$

${K}^{'} = 1 . 44K$.

So, the percentage change in kinetic energy
$= \dfrac{{K}^{'} - K}{K} \times 100$
$= \dfrac{1 . 44K - K}{K} \times 100$
$= \left(1 . 44 - 1\right) \times 100$
$= 44 %$.

49439.text: The angles of a triangle are in A.P and the greatest angle is double the least angle, then sine of the third angle is
49439.sol:
Let the angles of the triangle be $A-D$, $A$, and $A+D$.

The sum of the angles of a triangle is $180^{{}^{\circ}}$.

$(A-D) + A + (A+D) = 180^{{}^{\circ}}$

$3A = 180^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow A = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$

The greatest angle is double the least angle.

$A+D = 2(A-D)$

Substituting $A = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$:

$60^{{}^{\circ}}+D = 2(60^{{}^{\circ}}-D)$

$60^{{}^{\circ}}+D = 120^{{}^{\circ}}-2D$

$3D = 60^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow D = 20^{{}^{\circ}}$

The angles of the triangle are $40^{{}^{\circ}}$, $60^{{}^{\circ}}$, and $80^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The third angle (middle angle) is $60^{{}^{\circ}}$.

The sine of the third angle is $\sin 60^{{}^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

54433.subject: Physics
54433.text: $n$ small balls, each of mass $m$ impinge elastically each second on a surface with a velocity $u$, then the force experienced by the surface in one second, will be
54433.sol:
Force experienced by the surface is equal to change in momentum in one second.
From Newton's second law of motion, the rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the external force applied on the body and the change in momentum always takes place in the direction of the force.
Momentum of ball before impact $=m u$
Momentum after impact $=-m u$
Change in momentum $=m u-(-m u)=2 m u$
Change in momentum due to $n$ balls in one second is $=2 \mathrm{mnu}$.
Change of momentum = force experienced per second $=2 \mathrm{mnu}$.

54879.subject: Chemistry
54879.text: Which among the following compounds does NOT form inter molecular hydrogen bonding?
54879.sol:
Hydrogen bonding requires both a donor (H bonded to O, N, or F) and an acceptor (lone pair on O, N, or F).

Ethoxy ethane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2-O-CH_2CH_3}$) contains oxygen with lone pairs, acting as an acceptor, but lacks an H-donor group.

Butane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3}$) has no O, N, or F atoms—it cannot donate or accept hydrogen bonds.

Phenol ($\mathrm{C_6 H_5-OH}$) and bu\tan^{-1}-ol ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2 OH}$) both possess -OH groups, enabling donation and acceptance of hydrogen bonds.

Butane is uniquely incapable of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

56619.subject: Chemistry
56619.text: Which element from following has highest melting point?
56619.sol:
The melting point of transition metals depends on the strength of metallic bonding, which is directly proportional to the number of unpaired electrons available for bonding.

The electronic configurations of the given elements are:
$\text{V} : [\text{Ar}] 3d^3 4s^2$ (3$ unpaired electrons)
\text{Cr} : [\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$ (6$ unpaired electrons)
\text{Mn} : [\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$ (5$ unpaired electrons)
\text{Fe} : [\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$ (4$ unpaired electrons)

Chromium (Cr) has the maximum number of unpaired electrons (6$), which leads to the strongest metallic bonding among the given elements. Manganese (Mn) has an anomalously low melting point because its stable half-filled $3d^5$ configuration restricts the participation of electrons in metallic bonding.

Therefore, Cr has the highest melting point.

Answer: Cr

58035.subject: Chemistry
58035.text: The solubility of salt $\mathrm{BA}_2$ is $4 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{ mol } \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$. What is solubility product of the salt?
58035.sol:
Solubility product of $\mathrm{BA}_2$

The dissociation equilibrium is $\mathrm{BA}_2(s) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{B}^{2+}(aq) + 2\mathrm{A}^{-}(aq)$. The solubility product expression is $K_{sp} = [\mathrm{B}^{2+}][\mathrm{A}^{-}]^2$.

For a solubility of $s$, the ion concentrations are $[\mathrm{B}^{2+}] = s$ and $[\mathrm{A}^{-}] = 2s$. Substituting gives $K_{sp} = (s)(2s)^2 = 4s^3$.

Given $s = 4 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{dm}^{-3}$, we compute: $K_{sp} = 4 \times (4 \times 10^{-4})^3 = 4 \times (64 \times 10^{-12}) = 256 \times 10^{-12} = 2.56 \times 10^{-10}$.

This matches option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

58221.subject: Chemistry
58221.text: Which of the following noble gases exhibits higher oxidation states ?
58221.sol:
As we move down the group of noble gases, the atomic size increases and the ionization enthalpy decreases.

Xenon has a relatively low ionization enthalpy, which allows its valence electrons to be excited to empty d-orbitals.

This enables Xenon to form compounds with highly electronegative elements like fluorine and oxygen.

Xenon exhibits higher oxidation states such as $+2$, $+4$, $+6$, and $+8$ in compounds like $\text{XeF}_2$, $\text{XeF}_4$, $\text{XeF}_6$, $\text{XeO}_3$, and $\text{XeO}_4$.

Neon and Argon do not form stable compounds, and Krypton only forms $\text{KrF}_2$ with an oxidation state of $+2$.

Therefore, Xenon exhibits higher oxidation states.

Answer: Xe

59921.subject: Chemistry
59921.text: Calculate the work done in joule if 1 mole of ideal gas is compressed from $25 \mathrm{dm}^3$ to $13 \mathrm{dm}^3$ at constant external pressure 4 bar.
59921.sol:
Work done against constant external pressure is given by $W = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$.

Given $P_{\text{ext}} = 4\ \text{bar}$ with volume change $\Delta V = V_2 - V_1 = 13 - 25 = -12\ \text{dm}^3$.

Convert units to SI: $1\ \text{bar} = 10^5\ \text{Pa}$, so $P_{\text{ext}} = 4 \times 10^5\ \text{Pa}$.
Volume change: $1\ \text{dm}^3 = 10^{-3}\ \text{m}^3$, so $\Delta V = -12 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{m}^3$.

The work done becomes:
$W = -(4 \times 10^5) \times (-12 \times 10^{-3}) = (4 \times 10^5) \times (12 \times 10^{-3}) = 4800\ \text{J}$.

This positive value indicates work is done on the system during compression.

Final answer: $4800\ \text{J}$

60739.subject: Mathematics
60739.text: The number of common tangents that can be drawn to the circles $x^2+y^2-6 x=0$ and $x^2+y^2+6 x+2 y+1=0$ is.....
60739.sol:
Common tangents to two circles

The centers and radii of the circles are determined using the standard circle equation $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$.

For the first circle $x^2+y^2-6x=0$, the center is $C_1=(3,0)$ and radius $r_1=3$.

For the second circle $x^2+y^2+6x+2y+1=0$, the center is $C_2=(-3,-1)$ and radius $r_2=3$.

The distance between centers is $d=\sqrt{(-3-3)^2+(-1-0)^2}=\sqrt{37}$.

Since $d > r_1+r_2$ because $\sqrt{37}$> 6$, the circles lie completely outside each other.

Two non-intersecting circles have four common tangents: two direct and two transverse.

The number of common tangents is \boxed{4}$.

61698.sol:
Let $f(x) = 3x^3 + 2x^2 f'(1) + x f''(2) + f'''(3)$ and define constants $A = f'(1)$, $B = f''(2)$, and $C = f'''(3)$. The function becomes $f(x) = 3x^3 + 2Ax^2 + Bx + C$.

Successive differentiation yields:
$f'(x) = 9x^2 + 4Ax + B$,
$f''(x) = 18x + 4A$,
$f'''(x) = 18$.

Using the definitions of $A$, $B$, and $C$:
$A = 9 + 4A + B$ simplifies to $-3A - B = 9$,
$B = 36 + 4A$ gives $-4A + B = 36$,
and $C = 18$.

Solving the system $-3A - B = 9$ and $-4A + B = 36$:
Adding the equations eliminates $B$, resulting in $-7A = 45$, so $A = -\frac{45}{7}$.
Substituting into $-4A + B = 36$ gives $B = 36 - \frac{180}{7} = \frac{72}{7}$.

The function is thus $f(x) = 3x^3 - \frac{90}{7}x^2 + \frac{72}{7}x + 18 = \frac{21x^3 - 90x^2 + 72x + 126}{7}$, matching option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

65115.subject: Mathematics
65115.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ are non-coplanar unit vectors such that the angle between any two of them is $60^{}^{\circ}$, and the vector $\bar{d} = x\bar{a} + y\bar{b} + z\bar{c}$ is perpendicular to both $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, then the value of $\dfrac{(x+y)}{z}$ is
65115.sol:
Given $|\bar{a}| = |\bar{b}| = |\bar{c}| = 1$ and the angle between any two vectors is $60^{}^{\circ}$.

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = \bar{c} \cdot \bar{a} = 1 \times 1 \times \cos 60^{}^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Since $\bar{d}$ is perpendicular to $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, we have $\bar{d} \cdot \bar{a} = 0$ and $\bar{d} \cdot \bar{b} = 0$.

Substituting $\bar{d} = x\bar{a} + y\bar{b} + z\bar{c}$ into $\bar{d} \cdot \bar{a} = 0$:

$(x\bar{a} + y\bar{b} + z\bar{c}) \cdot \bar{a} = 0$

$x|\bar{a}|^2 + y(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a}) + z(\bar{c} \cdot \bar{a}) = 0$

$x(1) + y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + z\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0$

$2x + y + z = 0$

Similarly, substituting $\bar{d}$ into $\bar{d} \cdot \bar{b} = 0$:

$(x\bar{a} + y\bar{b} + z\bar{c}) \cdot \bar{b} = 0$

$x(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) + y|\bar{b}|^2 + z(\bar{c} \cdot \bar{b}) = 0$

$x\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + y(1) + z\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 0$

$x + 2y + z = 0$

Adding the two equations, we get:

$(2x + y + z) + (x + 2y + z) = 0$

$3x + 3y + 2z = 0$

$3(x + y) = -2z$

$\dfrac{x + y}{z} = -\dfrac{2}{3}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{2}{3}$

66040.text:
Two parallel plate air capacitors are connected in parallel. Each capacitor has plate area $A/2$ and separation between the plates is $d$ and $2d$ respectively. The equivalent capacity of the combination is

(\epsilon_0$ = absolute permittivity of free space)$
66040.sol:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is given by $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A'}{d'}$

For the first capacitor, area $A' = \dfrac{A}{2}$ and separation $d' = d$

$C_1 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{d} = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{2d}$

For the second capacitor, area $A' = \dfrac{A}{2}$ and separation $d' = 2d$

$C_2 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{2d} = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{4d}$

Since the capacitors are connected in parallel, their equivalent capacitance is the sum of their individual capacitances:

$C_{eq} = C_1 + C_2$

$C_{eq} = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{2d} + \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{4d} = \dfrac{3\epsilon_0 A}{4d}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3A\epsilon_0}{4d}$

67225.subject: Physics
67225.text: Two planets A and B have densities ${ }^{\prime} \varrho_1^{\prime},{ }^{\prime} \varrho_2^{\prime}$ and have radii ${ }^{\prime} \mathrm{r}_1^{\prime},{ }^{\prime} \mathrm{r}_2^{\prime}$ respectively. The ratio of acceleration due to gravity on $A$ to that of $B$ is
67225.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity at a planet's surface is $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$, where $G$ is the gravitational constant, $M$ is the planetary mass, and $R$ is the radius.
The mass can be expressed in terms of density $\varrho$ and volume as $M = \varrho V$.
For a spherical planet, $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3$, so $M = \frac{4}{3}\pi \varrho R^3$.

Substituting into the gravity formula yields $g = \frac{G \cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \varrho R^3}{R^2} = \frac{4}{3}\pi G \varrho R$.

For planet A: $g_A = \frac{4}{3}\pi G \varrho_1 r_1$
For planet B: $g_B = \frac{4}{3}\pi G \varrho_2 r_2$

The ratio simplifies to $\frac{g_A}{g_B} = \frac{\varrho_1 r_1}{\varrho_2 r_2}$.

The acceleration ratio is $r_1 \varrho_1 : r_2 \varrho_2$.

67403.text: A vessel has $6$ gram of hydrogen at pressure $P$ and temperature $500$ K. A small hole is made in it so that hydrogen leaks out. How much hydrogen leaks out if the final pressure is $\dfrac{P}{2}$ and the temperature falls to $300$ K?
67403.sol:
Using the ideal gas equation $PV = nRT = \dfrac{m}{M}RT$

Since the volume $V$ and molar mass $M$ remain constant, we have $P \propto mT$

$\dfrac{P_1}{P_2} = \dfrac{m_1 T_1}{m_2 T_2}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{P}{\dfrac{P}{2}} = \dfrac{6 \times 500}{m_2 \times 300}$

$2 = \dfrac{3000}{300 m_2}$

$2 = \dfrac{10}{m_2} \Rightarrow m_2 = 5$ g

The amount of hydrogen that leaks out is $\Delta m = m_1 - m_2 = 6 - 5 = 1$ g.

Answer: $1$ gram

67653.text: A charged particle is moving in a uniform magnetic field in a circular path of radius 'R'. When the energy of the particle becomes 3 times the original, the new radius will be
67653.sol:
The radius of a charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field is given by $R = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$.

The kinetic energy of the particle is $E = \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$, which gives the momentum $p = mv = \sqrt{2mE}$.

Substituting the momentum in the radius formula, we get $R = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mE}}{qB}$.

This shows that $R \propto \sqrt{E}$.

When the energy becomes $3$ times the original, the new energy is $E' = 3E$.

The new radius $R'$ is given by $R' = \dfrac{\sqrt{2m(3E)}}{qB} = \sqrt{3} \dfrac{\sqrt{2mE}}{qB} = \sqrt{3}R$.

Answer: $\sqrt{3}$R

The magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ is defined as $\chi = M/H$, where $M$ is magnetization and $H$ is magnetic field strength.

Paramagnetic materials exhibit atomic magnetic dipoles that align with an applied magnetic field, resulting in magnetization $M$ parallel to $H$. Since both quantities share the same direction, $\chi > 0$.

B) Negative and small – incorrect, diamagnetic property

$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Using } 3^{\text{rd }} \text{ equation$ of $motion, } \\ & \mathrm{v}^2=\mathrm{u}^2+2 \mathrm{as} \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{v}^2=2 \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{t}} \mathrm{s} \quad \ldots .(\text{ For } \mathrm{u}=0)\end{aligned}\therefore \quad \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2 \mathrm{ s}}$
By the end of $3^{\text{rd }}$ revolution, distance covered,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{s}=3(2 \pi \mathrm{r})=6 \pi \mathrm{r} \\
\therefore \quad & \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2}{2 \times 6 \pi \mathrm{r}}... (i)
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text{ Also, } \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=\mathrm{E} \\ \therefore \quad & \mathrm{v}^2=\frac{2 \mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{m}}... (ii)\end{aligned}$
Substituting equation (ii) in equation (i),
$a_t=\frac{2 E}{2 \times 6 \pi r \times m}=\frac{E}{6 \pi r m}$

69029.text: The size of the real image produced by a convex lens of focal length $\mathrm{F}$ is ' $\mathrm{m}$ ' times the size of the object. The image distance from the lens is
69029.sol:
From lens formula, $\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{ F}}$ For a convex lens, $\mathrm{u}$ is negative, $\mathrm{v}$ and $\mathrm{F}$ are positive. $\begin{aligned}& \therefore \quad \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}-\frac{1}{-\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{ F}}\\
& \therefore \quad \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{ F}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}
\end{aligned}$ Multiplying by $\mathrm{v}$, $\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{F}}-\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}\\
\therefore \quad 1 & =\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{F}}-\mathrm{m} \quad \ldots \left(\because \frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{u}}=\mathrm{m}\right)\\
\therefore \quad \frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{F}}& =1+\mathrm{m}\\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{v}& = \mathrm{F}(1+ \mathrm{m})
\end{aligned}$

69416.text: A semiconductor X is made by doping a germanium crystal with indium $(Z = 49)$. A second semiconductor Y is made by doping germanium crystal with arsenic $(Z = 33)$. Both are joined end to end and connected to a battery as shown. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: X is p-type, Y is n-type and the junction is forward biased.
X is p-type, Y is n-type and the junction is reverse biased.
X is n-type, Y is p-type and the junction is forward biased.
X is n-type, Y is p-type and the junction is reverse biased.
69416.sol:
Germanium is a Group 14 element with a valency of 4.

Semiconductor X is doped with Indium ($Z = 49$), which is a Group 13 element and a trivalent impurity. Doping a semiconductor with a trivalent impurity creates holes as majority charge carriers, making it a p-type semiconductor. Thus, X is p-type.

Semiconductor Y is doped with Arsenic ($Z = 33$), which is a Group 15 element and a pentavalent impurity. Doping with a pentavalent impurity provides extra electrons as majority charge carriers, making it an n-type semiconductor. Thus, Y is n-type.

In the given circuit diagram, the positive terminal of the battery (longer line) is connected to the p-type semiconductor (X), and the negative terminal (shorter, thicker line) is connected to the n-type semiconductor (Y).

When the p-side is connected to a higher potential than the n-side, the p-n junction is forward biased.

Therefore, X is p-type, Y is n-type, and the junction is forward biased.

Answer: X is p-type, Y is n-type and the junction is forward biased.

69470.subject: Physics
69470.text: The graph given below represents I - V characteristics of zener diode. The part of the characteristics curve that is most relevant for its operation as a voltage regulator is
69470.sol:
The current-voltage characteristics show distinct operational regions for the Zener diode. In forward bias, beyond the knee voltage (segment 'ab'), current increases exponentially with applied voltage, rendering this region unsuitable for voltage regulation. The near-origin region ('bc') represents transition behavior and is also irrelevant for regulation.

Under reverse bias, before breakdown occurs (segment 'cd'), only minimal leakage current flows while voltage increases negatively. This pre-breakdown region does not provide voltage regulation.

The key region is 'de', where Zener breakdown occurs. Here, the voltage remains nearly constant at the specified Zener voltage despite significant variations in reverse current. This characteristic of maintaining stable voltage under changing current conditions makes this region essential for voltage regulation applications.

71811.subject: Chemistry
71811.text: What is IUPAC name of Isoprene?
71811.sol:
Isoprene is the common name for the conjugated diene with the chemical formula $C_5H_8$.

The structure of isoprene is $CH_2=C(CH_3)-CH=CH_2$.

Selecting the longest carbon chain containing both double bonds gives a four-carbon chain (butadiene).

Numbering the chain to give the lowest locants to the double bonds and substituents, the double bonds are at positions 1 and 3, and the methyl group is at position 2.

Thus, the IUPAC name is 2-methyl-1,3-butadiene.

Answer: 2-methyl- 1, 3-butadine

71840.subject: Chemistry
71840.text: Which of the following reagent is NOT required for the conversion of propyne to acetone?
71840.sol:
The conversion of propyne to acetone is achieved by the hydration of an alkyne (Kucherov reaction).

The reagents used for this reaction are water, dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and $\text{HgSO}_4$.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C} \equiv \text{CH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HgSO}_4, \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} [\text{CH}_3-\text{C(OH)}=\text{CH}_2] \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$

Zinc dust is not required for this conversion. It is typically used in reactions like reductive ozonolysis or dehalogenation.

Answer: Zinc dust

71961.text: A metal crystallizes in FCC crystal lattice with density 10 $\text{g/cm}^3$. The edge length of unit cell is 100 pm. The number of unit cell present in 100 g of metal is-
71961.sol:
Volume of the metal = $\dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} = \dfrac{100}{10} = 10 \text{ cm}^3$

Edge length of unit cell, $a = 100 \text{ pm} = 10^{-8} \text{ cm}$

Volume of one unit cell = $a^3 = (10^{-8})^3 = 10^{-24} \text{ cm}^3$

Number of unit cells = $\dfrac{\text{Total volume}}{\text{Volume of one unit cell}} = \dfrac{10}{10^{-24}} = 1 \times 10^{25}$

Answer: $1 \times 10^{25}$

72062.subject: Chemistry
72062.text: What is the work done when an ideal gas (0.300 mol) expands in vacuum?
72062.sol:
Work done during the expansion of a gas is given by the expression $W = -P_{ext} \Delta V$.

For expansion in a vacuum (free expansion), the external pressure $P_{ext}$ is zero.

Substituting $P_{ext} = 0$ in the expression for work done, we get $W = 0$.

Thus, the work done when an ideal gas expands in a vacuum is zero.

Answer: zero

76573.text: Which one of the following is the greatest coefficient in the expansion of $(1 + x)^{100}$?
76573.sol:
The general term in the expansion of $(1 + x)^{n}$ is given by $T_{r+1} = ^{n}C_{r} x^{r}$, where the coefficient of $x^{r}$ is ^{n}C_{r}$.

For an even integer $n$, the greatest binomial coefficient is the middle term, which is ^{n}C_{n/2}$.

Given $n = 100$, which is even, the greatest coefficient is ^{100}C_{100/2} = ^{100}C_{50}$.

This corresponds to the coefficient of $x^{50}$.

Answer: The coefficient of $x^{50}

77328.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
A function $f$ is such that $f(xy) = f(x+y)$ for all real values of $x$ and $y$, and $f(5) = 10$.

What is $f(0)$ equal to?
77328.sol:
Given the functional equation $f(xy) = f(x+y)$ for all real values of $x$ and $y$.

Substituting $y = 0$ into the given equation:

$f(x \cdot 0) = f(x + 0)$

$f(0) = f(x)$

This shows that $f(x)$ is a constant function, meaning it takes the same value for all real $x$.

We are given that $f(5) = 10$.

Since $f(x) = f(0)$ for all $x$, substituting $x = 5$ gives:

$f(5) = f(0)$

Therefore, $f(0) = 10$.

Answer: $10$

77363.text: If $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow S$ defined by $f(x)=4 \sin x-3 \cos x+1$ is onto, then what is $S$ equal to?
77363.sol:
$f(x)=4 \sin x-3 \cos x+1$
To find range of this function, we have to find maximum and minimum values.
We know, for a $\sin \theta+\mathrm{b} \cos \theta+\mathrm{c}$, max value is $\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}+\mathrm{c}$ and minimum value is $-\sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2}+\mathrm{c}$.
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \text{ Maximum value } & =\sqrt{(4)^2+(-3)^2}+1 \\
& =\sqrt{16+9}+1=5+1=6
\end{aligned}$
Minimum value $=-\sqrt{16+9+1}=-5+1=-4\therefore$ Range, $\mathrm{S} \in[-4,6]$

78925.subject: Mathematics
78925.text: If $0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then what is the number of values of $x$ satisfying the equation $\tan x + \sec x = 2\cos x$?
78925.sol:
The given equation is $\tan x + \sec x = 2\cos x$.

Rewriting the equation in terms of $\sin x and \cos x$:

$\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{1}{\cos x} = 2\cos x$

For the equation to be defined, $\cos x \neq 0$, which means $x \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Thus, $x \in \left[$0, $\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).

Multiplying both sides by $\cos x$:

$\sin x + 1 = 2\cos^2 x$

Substituting $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$:

$\sin x + 1 = 2(1 - \sin^2 x)$

$2\sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0$

Factoring the quadratic equation:

$(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1) = 0$

This gives $\sin x = $\dfrac{1}{2}$ or \sin x = -1$.

Since $x \in $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\sin x \geq 0$. Therefore, $\sin x = -1$ is rejected.

For $\sin x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, the only solution in the given interval is $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Thus, there is exactly $1$ value of $x$ satisfying the equation.

Answer: $1$

79492.text: The characteristics of class Reptilia are
options: body covered with moist skin which is devoid of scales, the ear is represented by a tympanum, alimentary canal, urinary and reproductive tracts open into a common cloaca.

79492.sol:
Characteristics of class Reptilia:
1. Creeping and burrowing terrestrial animals with scales on their body, skin is dry, and rough, without any glands.
2. Cold-blooded animals; exhibit a meroblastic segmentation.
3. Few of these shed the scales on their skin as skin cast.
4. Respiration by lungs.
5. Two pairs of pentadactyl limbs, each bearing claws. Snakes are an exception.
6. Heart is 3 chambered. However, crocodiles have a 4-chambered heart.
7. Nervous system comprises of 12 pairs of cranial nerves, lateral line system is absent.
8. Except for snakes, all the reptiles have well-developed ears.
9. possess a typical cloaca.
10. Reptiles are ureotelic, uricotelic, and ammoniotelic.
11. Fertilization is internal; oviparous and the eggs are very yolky

& C_P=C_1+C_2=16(2) \\

& C_1 C_2=48 \\

& C_2=16-\left(48 / C_2\right) \\

& \therefore C_2^2+48-16 C_2=0 \\
& \therefore C_2=12 \mu F, C_2=4 \mu F
\end{aligned}\)

So for $A, {N}_{A} = {N}_{0}{e}^{- 8\lambdat}$

for $B, {N}_{B} = {N}_{0}{e}^{- \lambdat}$

given $\dfrac{{N}_{A}}{{N}_{B}} = \dfrac{1}{e}$

Then

$\dfrac{{N}_{A}}{{N}_{B}} = \dfrac{{N}_{0}{e}^{- 8\lambdat}}{{N}_{0}{e}^{- \lambdat}}$

$\dfrac{1}{e} = {e}^{- 7\lambdat}$

$- 1 = - 7\lambdat$

$t = \dfrac{1}{7\lambda}$

Reproductive individuals are less than the post-reproductive individuals
Pre-reproductive individuals are more than reproductive individuals
Pre-reproductive individuals are less than the reproductive individuals

90926.text: A man is walking towards a vertical pillar in a straight path at a uniform speed. At a certain point $A$ on the path, he observes that the angle of elevation of the top of the pillar is ${30}^{o} .$ After walking for $5\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)$ minutes from $A$ in the same direction, at a point $B$, he observes that the angle of elevation of the top of the pillar is ${45}^{o} .$ Then the time taken (in minutes) by him, to reach from $B$ to the pillar, is (take $\sqrt{3} = 1 .73$)
90926.sol:
In $∆ QPA: \dfrac{h}{x + y} = tan ⁡ {30}^{o} ⇒ \sqrt{3}h = x + y \ldots \ldots .(i)$
In $∆ QPB: \dfrac{h}{y} = tan ⁡ {45}^{o} ⇒ h = y \ldots \ldots .(ii)$
From (i) and (ii), we get,

$\sqrt{3} y = x + y ⇒ y = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$
Given that the distance $x$ is covered in $5\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)$ minutes
Hence, the distance $\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$ is covered in $\dfrac{5\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)}{\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right)} = 5\left(2 + \sqrt{3}\right) = 18 . 65$ minutes

93310.text: A large sphere of mass $M$ is fixed at one position and two identical particles each of mass $m$ are kept on a line passing through the centre of $M$ (see figure). The point masses are connected by a rigid massless rod of length $l$ and this assembly is free to move along the line connecting them. All three masses interact only through their mutual gravitational interaction. When the point mass nearer to $M$ is at a distance $r = 3l$ from $M$, the tension in the rod is zero for $m = k\left(\dfrac{M}{288}\right)$. The value of $k$ is
93310.sol:
Due to gravitational interaction connected masses have some acceleration.

Let both small masses are moving with acceleration 'a' towards larger mass M



Force equation for mass nearer to a larger mass

$\dfrac{GMm}{{\left(3l\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{G{m}^{2}}{{l}^{2}} = ma$ ...(i)

Force equation for mass away from a larger mass

$\dfrac{GMm}{{\left(4l\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{G{m}^{2}}{{l}^{2}} = ma$ ...(ii)

From equation (i) & (ii)

$\dfrac{GM}{9{l}^{2}} - \dfrac{Gm}{{l}^{2}} = \dfrac{GM}{16{l}^{2}} + \dfrac{Gm}{{l}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{M}{9} - \dfrac{M}{16} = m + m$

$\dfrac{7M}{144} = 2m$

$⇒ m = \dfrac{7M}{288} = k\left(\dfrac{M}{288}\right)$

$⇒ k = 7$

96265.text:
Match the following column I with column II.
&
Column – I Column – II
A. Metaphase - II 1. Centromere with 2 kinetochores
B. Anaphase - I 2. Disjunction
C. Mitosis 3. Synapse
D. Zygotene 4. Plectonemic coiling
96265.sol:
The chromosomes become arranged on the metaphase plate, much as the chromosomes do in mitosis, and are attached to the now fully formed spindle. In metaphase II, the centromeres contain two kinetochores that attach to spindle fibers from the centrosomes at opposite poles. The new equatorial metaphase plate is rotated by 90 degrees when compared to meiosis I, perpendicular to the previous plate.
Disjunction of chromosomes takes place in anaphase-I and II when chromosomes move to the opposite poles of the cell.

Plectonemic coiling refers to inter-twining of a double helix DNA molecule in such a way that for its correction unwinding of DNA helix molecule is required, this take place in mitosis in which sister chromatids are tightly coiled upon each other. In the zygotene stage, homologs login to synapse by coming to approximate alignment.

97345.sol: Abscisic acid stimulates senescence of leaves by causing destruction of chlorophyll and inhibition of protein and RNA synthesis.& It acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. ABA inhibits seed germination. ABA stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses. Therefore, it is also called the stress hormone. ABA plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy. By inducing dormancy, ABA helps seeds to withstand desiccation and other factors unfavourable for growth. In most situations, ABA acts as an antagonist to GAs.

97367.text: Which of the following plants requires light exposure less than the critical period to initiate flowering?
97367.sol: The critical photoperiod is the light period required for floral induction, which must not be exceeded in short-day plants and should always be exceeded in long day plants in order to bring them to flower. Tobacco is a short-day plant (SDP). When the photoperiod is less than the critical period plant will flower. Wheat, Spinach and oat are all long-day plants (LDP), which flower when they receive photoperiod or light hours above the critical photoperiod.

97954.subject: Botany
97954.text: Exudation and guttation are due to
97954.sol:
Osmotic pressure developed in the cells of roots in the root system is termed as root pressure and this supports in the rise of the cell sap towards the leaves. Root pressure results in exudation and as well as guttation.

Fluid emitted via the roots of the plants are referred to as exudates and the process is called as exudation.

Loss of impure water from plant, generally from the margins of leaves is termed as guttation. The water contains a dilute solution of different organic and inorganic substances. Guttation occurs due to low rate of transpiration and more water absorption. This higher rate of absorption develops root pressure and pushes the excess water out of the specialized pores of veins called hydathodes. Guttation is a type of exudation.

98320.sol: Carbohydrates are hydrates of carbon. These are classified as Monosaccharides, Oligosaccharides and Polysaccharides. Polysaccharides can be homopolysaccharides if these are made up of same sugar unit and are heteropolysaccharides if these have more than one sugar unit. Examples of homopolysaccharides are Starch, Glycogen, Cellulose, Chitin, etc. Glycogen is made up of many glucose units. It is the stored form of sugar in animals and hence is also known as animal starch. In the structure, the right end is known as reducing end and the left end is non reducing end. Reducing sugars have free aldehyde or ketone group, while non-reducing sugars have no free group. Glycogen has no free groups and hence are reducing sugars.

98341.text: Select the option which is not correct with respect to enzyme action.

Addition of lot of succinate does not reverse the inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate.
A noncompetitive inhibitor cannot bind the active site of the enzyme at a site distinct from that which binds the substrate.
Malonate is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase.
98341.sol: The reduction of activity of succinate dehydrogenase by malonate is an example of competitive inhibition. Competitive inhibition is a reversible inhibition where inhibitor competes with the normal substrate for the active site of the enzyme. A competitive inhibitor is usually similar to the normal substrate and, therefore, fits the active site of an enzyme and binds with it. Since a competitive inhibitor occupies the site only temporarily, the enzyme action is not permanently affected. Thus, addition of a lot of succinate can reverse the inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate.

100439.subject: Physics
100439.text:
The equation of motion of a projectile is $y=a x-b x^2$, where $a, b$ are constants. Match the column - I with column - II
$\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Column - I} & \text{Column - II} \\
\text{i) The initial velocity of projection} & \text{a)} \frac{a}{b} \\
\text{ii) The horizontal range of projectile} & \text{b)} a \sqrt{\frac{2}{\mathrm{bg}}} \\
\text{iii) The maximum height attained by projectile} & \text{c)} \frac{\mathrm{a}^2}{4 \mathrm{ b}} \\
\text{iv) The time of flight of projectile} & \text{d)} \sqrt{\frac{g\left(1+a^2\right)}{2 b}}
\end{array}$
options: $\begin{array}{cccc}\text{ i } & \text{ ii } & \text{ iii } & \text{ iv } \\ \text{ a } & \text{ d } & \text{ c } & \text{ b }\end{array}$
100439.sol:
Matching the Columns
i) The initial velocity of projection
From our derivation, \(u=$\sqrt{\frac{g\left(1+a^2\right)}{2 b}}$.
This matches option d.
ii) The horizontal range of a projectile
The horizontal range, \(R\), is the value of \(x\) when \(y=0\).
\(y=a x-b x²=x(a-b x)=0\)
The solutions are \(x=0\) and \(x=$\frac{a}{b}$. The range is the non-zero solution.
\(R=$\frac{a}{b} .$
This matches option a.
iii) The maximum height attained by the projectile
The maximum height, \(H\), occurs at the midpoint of the range, so at \(x=R / 2=$\frac{a}{2 b}$.
Substitute this into the trajectory equation:
\(H=a$\left(\frac{a}{2 b}\right)-$b$\left(\frac{a}{2 b}\right)^$2=$\frac{a^2}{2 b}-$b$\left(\frac{a^2}{4 b^2}\right)=\frac{a^2}{2 b}-\frac{a^2}{4 b}=\frac{2 a^2-a^2}{4 b}=\frac{a^2}{4 b} .This matches option c.
iv) The $time of flight of the projectile
The time of flight, \(T\), is related to the range by the horizontal velocity: \(R=u \cos$\theta \cdot$T\).
\(T=$\frac{R}{u \cos \theta}=\frac{a / b}{u / \sqrt{1+\tan ^2 \theta}}=\frac{a}{b} \frac{\sqrt{1+\alpha^2}}{u} .$
Substitute our expression for \(u\) :
\(T=$\frac{a}{b} \frac{\sqrt{1+a^2}}{\sqrt{\frac{\left(1+a^2\right)}{2}}}=\frac{a}{b} \sqrt{\frac{\left(1+a^2\right) 2 b}{g\left(1+a^2\right)}}=\frac{a}{b} \sqrt{\frac{2 b}{g}}=\frac{a \sqrt{2 b}}{b \sqrt{g}}=\frac{a}{b} \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{b} \sqrt{g}}=\frac{a \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{b} \sqrt{g}}=$a $\sqrt{\frac{2}{b g}} .$
This matches option b.
Final Matches
- i \( → \) d
- ii \( → \) a
- iii \( → c\)
- iv \( → \) b
This matches the configuration of option (3).

100886.subject: Physics
100886.text:
A car of mass $2000$ kg moves up a rough inclined plane at a constant speed of $10$ m/s. The incline makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal such that $\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{20}$. If the constant frictional force acting on the car is $500$ N, the power output of the car's engine is :
($g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
100886.sol:
Since the car moves at a constant speed, its acceleration is zero, meaning the net force acting on it is zero.

The driving force $F$ provided by the engine must balance both the downward component of gravity along the incline and the opposing frictional force $f$.

$F = mg \sin\theta + f$

$F = \left(2000 \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{20}\right) + 500$

$F = 1000 + 500 = 1500$ N.

The power output of the engine is given by the product of the driving force and the velocity.

$P = F \times v$

$P = 1500 \times 10 = 15000$ W.

$P = 15$ kW.

Answer: $15$ kW

101393.subject: Physics
101393.text: Two point masses $M$ and $16M$ are fixed at a separation distance of $10a$. A small particle is released from rest at the point on the line joining them where the net gravitational field is zero. What is the minimum speed the particle must be given at this point so that it escapes to infinity?
101393.sol:
Let the neutral point be at a distance $x$ from the mass $M$.

Equating the magnitudes of the gravitational fields due to both masses:
$\dfrac{GM}{x^2} = \dfrac{G(16M)}{(10a-x)^2}$

Taking the square root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{4}{10a-x}$
$\Rightarrow 10a - x = 4x \Rightarrow 5x = 10a \Rightarrow x = 2a$

The distance of this neutral point from the mass $16M$ is $10a - 2a = 8a$.

The net gravitational potential $V$ at this neutral point is:
$V = -\dfrac{GM}{2a} - \dfrac{G(16M)}{8a}$
$V = -\dfrac{GM}{2a} - \dfrac{2GM}{a} = -\dfrac{5GM}{2a}$

To escape to infinity, the total mechanical energy of the particle must be at least zero. By conservation of mechanical energy:
$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + mV = 0$
$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + m\left(-\dfrac{5GM}{2a}\right) = 0$
$\dfrac{1}{2}v^2 = \dfrac{5GM}{2a}$
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{5GM}{a}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{5GM}{a}}$

101961.text: The temperature of inversion of a thermocouple is $620^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and the neutral temperature is $300^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, what is the temperature of cold junction?
101961.sol:
The temperature of inversion is higher than the neutral temperature by the same amount as the neutral temperature is higher than the temperature of cold junction.
As per Key Idea
$t_n-t_0=t_i-t_n \Rightarrow t_0=2 t_n-t_i$
Given, $t_i=620^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, t_n=300^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
Hence, $t_0=$ temperature of cold junction
$\begin{aligned} & =2 \times 300-620 \\ & =600-620=-20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
NOTE: Neutral temperature does not change for a metal whether the temperature of cold junction and inversion temperature change by any value.

103853.text:
The induced emf can be produced in a coil by

A. moving the coil with uniform speed inside uniform magnetic field

B. moving the coil with non uniform speed inside uniform magnetic field

C. rotating the coil inside the uniform magnetic field

D. changing the area of the coil inside the uniform magnetic field

103853.sol:
Induced emf is given by Faraday's law

$\left|ε\right| = \dfrac{dϕ}{dt}$

where $ϕ$ is the magnetic flux.

The rate of change of flux through a circuit is defined as emf. The formula for flux is $ϕ = \overset{\to}{B} \cdot \overset{\to}{A}$. In the statements $A \text{ and } B$ given in the question, the magnetic flux in the coil in uniform magnetic field does not change. So, no emf is induced.

But in statement $C$, the angle between the area vector and the magnetic field continuously changes hence, an emf is generated. In statement $D$, the area is changing in unit time so magnetic flux will change and an emf is generated.

104111.subject: Physics
104111.text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an AC source $V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin(1000 t)$ Volts. The current amplitude in the circuit is $2$ A. Given that $R = 50 \, \Omega$, $L = 100$ mH, and the voltage leads the current, the value of capacitance $C$ is :
104111.sol:
From the given voltage equation $V = 100\sqrt{2} \sin(1000 t)$, the peak voltage is $V_m = 100\sqrt{2}$ V and the angular frequency is $\omega = 1000$ rad/s.

The impedance of the circuit is given by $Z = \dfrac{V_m}{I_m} = \dfrac{100\sqrt{2}}{2} = 50\sqrt{2} \, \Omega$.

Using the impedance formula $Z^2 = R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2$, we have:
$(50\sqrt{2})^2 = 50^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2$
$5000 = 2500 + (X_L - X_C)^2$
$(X_L - X_C)^2 = 2500 \implies |X_L - X_C| = 50 \, \Omega$

The inductive reactance is $X_L = \omega L = 1000 \times (100 \times 10^{-3}) = 100 \, \Omega$.

Since the voltage leads the current, the circuit is inductive, which means $X_L > X_C$.
Therefore, $X_L - X_C = 50 \implies 100 - X_C = 50 \implies X_C = 50 \, \Omega$.

The capacitance is $C = \dfrac{1}{\omega X_C} = \dfrac{1}{1000 \times 50} = \dfrac{1}{50000} = 20 \times 10^{-6}$ F $= 20 \, \mu$F.

Answer: $20 \, \mu$F

107788.subject: Chemistry
107788.text:
Consider the following chemical species :
$\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$, $\mathrm{I_3^-}$, $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{PCl_3}$

How many of the given species have a planar structure?
107788.sol:
To determine if a species is planar, we first find its hybridisation, number of bond pairs (bp), and lone pairs (lp) on the central atom using VSEPR theory.

$\mathrm{XeF_4}$ : Central atom Xe has 8 valence electrons. It forms 4 sigma bonds with F and has 2 lone pairs. Steric number = 6 ($sp^3d^2$). The shape is square planar, which is planar.

$\mathrm{ClF_3}$ : Central atom Cl has 7 valence electrons. It forms 3 sigma bonds with F and has 2 lone pairs. Steric number = 5 ($sp^3d$). The shape is T-shaped, which is planar.

$\mathrm{I_3^-}$ : Central atom I has 7 valence electrons + 1 (negative charge) = 8 electrons. It forms 2 sigma bonds with the other two I atoms and has 3 lone pairs. Steric number = 5 ($sp^3d$). The shape is linear, which is planar.

$\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$ : Central atom C forms 3 sigma bonds (and 1 pi bond) with no lone pairs. Steric number = 3 ($sp^2$). The shape is trigonal planar, which is planar.

$\mathrm{SF_4}$ : Central atom S has 6 valence electrons. It forms 4 sigma bonds and has 1 lone pair. Steric number = 5 ($sp^3d$). The shape is see-saw, which is non-planar.

$\mathrm{PCl_3}$ : Central atom P has 5 valence electrons. It forms 3 sigma bonds and has 1 lone pair. Steric number = 4 ($sp^3$). The shape is trigonal pyramidal, which is non-planar.

Thus, there are 4 planar species : $\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$, $\mathrm{I_3^-}$, and $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$.

Answer: 4

111950.subject: Chemistry
111950.text: Among the following substituted cyclohexyl carbocations, which one is stabilized by the maximum number of hyperconjugative structures?
111950.sol:
The number of hyperconjugative structures for a carbocation is equal to the number of $\alpha$-hydrogens attached to the positively charged carbon.

For the 1-methylcyclohexyl cation, the positively charged carbon is attached to a methyl group (which provides 3 $\alpha$-hydrogens) and two adjacent ring carbons (which provide 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens each). Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $3 + 2 + 2 = 7$.

For the 1-ethylcyclohexyl cation, the ethyl group provides 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens. Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $2 + 4 = 6$.

For the 1-isopropylcyclohexyl cation, the isopropyl group provides 1 $\alpha$-hydrogen. Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $1 + 4 = 5$.

For the 1-tert-butylcyclohexyl cation, the tert-butyl group provides 0 $\alpha$-hydrogens. Total $\alpha$-hydrogens = $0 + 4 = 4$.

Therefore, the 1-methylcyclohexyl cation has the maximum number of $\alpha$-hydrogens and is stabilized by the maximum number of hyperconjugative structures.

Answer: 1-Methylcyclohexyl cation

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Copper(I) ion is unstable in aqueous solution and undergoes disproportionation to Copper(II) ion and solid copper.
Reason (R): Copper(II) ion has a more stable $3d^9$ electronic configuration compared to the completely filled $3d^{10}$ configuration of Copper(I) ion.

options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
117130.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. In aqueous solutions, $Cu^+$ undergoes disproportionation: $2Cu^+_{(aq)} \rightarrow Cu^{2+}_{(aq)} + Cu_{(s)}$.

Reason (R) is false. The $Cu^+$ ion has a completely filled $3d^{10}$ configuration, which is electronically more stable than the $3d^9$ configuration of $Cu^{2+}$. The instability of $Cu^+$ in aqueous solution is not due to its electronic configuration, but rather because the high negative hydration enthalpy of the $Cu^{2+}$ ion more than compensates for the second ionization enthalpy of copper.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

121772.subject: Botany
121772.text: How do antherozoids reach the archegonium?
121772.sol: Bryophytes include the various mosses and liverworts that are found commonly growing in moist shaded areas in the hills. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction. They usually occur in damp, humid and shaded localities. They play an important role in plant succession on bare rocks/soil. The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. They lack true roots, stems or leaves. They may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures. The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes, hence is called a gametophyte. The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular. The male sex organ is called antheridium. They produce biflagellate antherozoids. The female sex organ called archegonium is flask-shaped and produces a single egg. <mark>The antherozoids are released into water where they come in contact with archegonium.</mark> An antherozoid fuses with the egg to produce the zygote. Zygotes do not undergo reduction division immediately. They produce a multicellular body called a sporophyte. The sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo reduction division (meiosis) to produce haploid spores. These spores germinate to produce gametophyte.
121772.meta: How do antherozoids reach the archegonium?

121796.subject: Botany
121796.text: What are the three parts of the sporophyte in liverworts?
121796.sol: The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid, e.g., Marchantia. The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures. Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialized structures called gemmae (sing. gemma). Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli. The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals. During sexual reproduction, male and female sex organs are produced either on the same or on different thalli. <mark>The sporophyte is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule.</mark> After meiosis, spores are produced within the capsule. These spores germinate to form free-living gametophytes.

122203.subject: Botany
122203.text: What are the two basic body forms of cnidarians?
122203.sol: Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic. Cnidoblasts, also known as cnidocytes, contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture in cnidarians. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Some of the cnidarians, e.g., corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa (Figure 4.6). The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

122759.subject: Botany
122759.text: In which type of placentation do the ovules borne on the central axis and septa are absent?
122759.sol: The arrangement of ovules within the ovary is known as placentation. The placentation are of different types namely, marginal, axile, parietal, basal, central and free central (Figure 5.12). In marginal placentation the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows, as in pea. When the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, the placentaion is said to be axile, as in china rose, tomato and lemon. In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part. Ovary is one-chambered but it becomes twochambered due to the formation of the false septum, e.g., mustard and Argemone. When the ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and Primrose the placentation is called free central. In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of ovary and a single ovule is attached to it, as in sunflower, marigold.

123613.sol: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores.
